title: How many ways can three blanks give a median of thirteen?
description: Three blanks follow the numbers five, twenty one and fourteen, and the median of all six must be thirteen. The third and fourth sorted values must add to twenty six, and one blank can grow without end.
teaching_notes: One idea: for six values the median is the average of the third and fourth sorted values, so those two must add to twice the median. Watch for students who count only the few lists they tried and say the number of ways is small.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 3)
video_script.why: A child who finds a median from two middle values now works backwards from the median to fill blanks.
video_script.substitution: the book's numbers 5, 21 and 14 with three blanks and the median 13
video_script.anchor: a row of six boxes holding 5, 21, 14 and three blanks
never_show: a finite count of possibilities, marked as right
maths_rules: 6 values: median = average of the 3rd and 4th sorted values; median 13 means they add to 26
blanks 3, 12 and any n at least 14: sorted 3, 5, 12, 14, ... with n and 21 after, so the 3rd and 4th stay 12 and 14; n can be 14, 15, 16, ... without end
video_script.design: One row of six boxes all video. Each fill of the blanks is sorted in front of the child and the third and fourth boxes are marked, so the sum twenty six is seen directly.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many ways are there if only counting numbers are allowed?

<bookmark mark='pair'/>Twelve and fourteen add to twenty six, so the median is thirteen.
